exact_statement: On the uniform six-dimensional Boolean cube, let a selected physical coordinate have four pivotal pairs whose five-dimensional child locations form an affine two-plane. If the child sign on this plane is bent, and zero through six of the other seven parallel slices are affine (the rest bent), then its spectral erasure satisfies B_i<=4 Inf_i=1/2. For seven affine slices this assertion fails: the saved actual Boolean truth table has B_i=(136 log2(17)+120 log2(5)-704)/256>1/2, H=21/4 and I=9/4, with a K4-good alternative physical coordinate. Its exact nearest quadratic distances are 12 without a polar constraint and 14 when the selected quadratic polar row is nonzero. For any quadratic phase on six physical controls edited at at most twelve vertices, a nonzero polar coordinate with four pivotal pairs is K4-good whenever the surviving pivotal child set is an affine two-plane. All affine-phase mask terminals with at most twelve edits on D>=6 controls retain the unchanged K=4+2/ln(2) payment. Consequently the inherited physical stopping policy extends at the same K through twelve coherent same-fiber edits conditional on every reached four-pair critical node having planar surviving pivotal set; the general affine-span-three critical case remains open.
hypotheses: Boolean signs on a uniform physical cube; entropy and erasure in bits; exact Fourier probabilities.
Affine changes of unqueried coordinates are used solely to preserve the selected coordinate erasure and influence, never to transport another physical influence.
The twelve-edit node lemma requires a nonzero selected quadratic polar row and an affine two-plane surviving pivotal set.
The twelve-edit stopping consequence is conditional on planar critical nodes at every reached restriction and uses the complete inherited five-control, JS and terminal proofs.
